s1.syndrome_frame: a postmenopausal woman with a long-standing, progressively enlarging breast mass associated with skin ulceration
salient_findings: skin ulceration over the breast mass
hard, non-tender, and mobile breast mass
key_facts: 56-year-old postmenopausal woman
right breast mass noted for more than 1 year
mass gradually enlarged
mass is hard in texture
mass is non-tender
mass is mobile
skin ulceration with mild exudation and bleeding
breast ultrasound classified the lesion as BI-RADS category V
breast MRI classified the lesion as BI-RADS category V
chest CT demonstrated a right breast mass suggestive of malignancy
serum breast tumor markers were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common type of breast cancer, consistent with long-standing, enlarging mass and skin ulceration

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: aggressive type of breast cancer, consistent with skin ulceration and rapid progression

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: rare type of breast cancer, consistent with skin ulceration and nipple-areolar complex involvement

shortlist.label: Metaplastic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: rare, aggressive type of breast cancer, consistent with skin ulceration and poor prognosis

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: rare, aggressive type of breast cancer, consistent with skin ulceration and rapid progression

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a hard, non-tender, and mobile mass, along with skin ulceration and a BI-RADS category V classification on both ultrasound and MRI, is most consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma, which is the most common type of breast cancer and can cause skin changes and masses as described.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: Typically presents with rapid onset of erythema and edema, which is not the primary complaint here

rejected.label: Paget's disease of the breast
rejected.why: Usually involves the nipple-areolar complex and presents with eczematous changes, not a large mass with ulceration

rejected.label: Metaplastic carcinoma
rejected.why: Less common and often has a more aggressive appearance on imaging, but the clinical presentation here does not specifically suggest this subtype

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma of the breast
rejected.why: Rare and typically presents as a rapidly growing mass, but the imaging and clinical findings do not specifically point to a vascular tumor
